question_text: A 30-year-old boxer seeks evaluation by his physician after he noticed swelling at the angle of his jaw a few days ago. He recalls a recent boxing match when he was punched in his face. He says that his jaw is very painful. On examination, a firm mass is palpated, measuring 4 x 4 cm. An ultrasound was performed, which shows a thin, encapsulated, well-circumscribed, predominantly solid mass with occasional cystic areas. The mass is surgically excised, after which he develops a hoarse voice for a few days, but recovers within 1 week. The histopathologic evaluation of the surgical specimen reports a pseudocapsule with a hypocellular stromal component consisting of a myxoid background and cartilage arranged in clusters and a hypercellular epithelial component with cells arranged in sheets and trabeculae. From which of the following structures did the mass most likely arise?
